objects.description: Function type for abort hooks. Functions of this type take no parameters and return no value; they can be registered via AtAbort to be invoked when Abort is called.

functions.name: Abort
functions.description: Terminates the process immediately. Likely invokes any functions registered via AtAbort() before exiting. This function does not return.
requirements: May be called at any time; it never returns
Side effects: process termination; any registered abort hooks may run

functions.name: AtAbort
functions.description: Registers a callback (abort hook) to be invoked when Abort() is called. Use to perform last-chance logging or cleanup steps that are safe during abort.
requirements: The callback pointer must be non-null
The callback must be async-signal-safe and reentrant if Abort() can occur from signal/undefined states (exact guarantees unknown)
Registration order and lifetime semantics are not documented; multiple registrations may be allowed but are unspecified

functions.name: GetStartDir
functions.description: Returns the process' starting/initial working directory as a string. Ownership and allocation details are not documented; likely returns a heap-allocated, NUL-terminated path string.
requirements: Caller must treat the returned pointer as a NUL-terminated C string
Memory ownership/need to free is unknown; verify in implementation before freeing or retaining

functions.name: GetOpt
functions.description: Parses command-line options similarly to getopt(), using the global variables optind_ and optarg_. Pass argc, argv, and an option string to control parsing.
requirements: argv must be a valid array of pointers to NUL-terminated strings, of length argc
optstring must be a non-null NUL-terminated string describing valid options
Relies on extern globals optind_ and optarg_; callers must observe and/or reset optind_ as needed between parses
Thread safety is unknown; avoid concurrent use without external synchronization

functions.name: tpenc
functions.description: Encodes a 32-bit value (likely a Unicode code point) into a packed 64-bit representation suitable for text processing. Specific encoding details and error conventions are not documented.
requirements: Input value semantics are unknown; if representing a Unicode code point, it should be a valid scalar value
Returned 64-bit value encoding/usage is unspecified; consult implementation before interpreting or storing

functions.name: DescribeSignal
functions.description: Returns a descriptive name or message string for a POSIX signal number.
requirements: Signal number may be any int; out-of-range values may yield a generic/unknown description
Returned pointer refers to a NUL-terminated string with lifetime managed by the library (do not free)

functions.name: DescribeHostErrno
functions.description: Returns a descriptive name or message string for a host errno value.
requirements: Errno value may be any int; unrecognized values may yield a generic/unknown description
Returned pointer refers to a NUL-terminated string with library-managed lifetime (do not free)

functions.name: EndsWith
functions.description: Returns true if the first NUL-terminated string ends with the specified suffix.
requirements: Both input pointers must be non-null and point to NUL-terminated strings

functions.name: StartsWith
functions.description: Returns true if the first NUL-terminated string begins with the specified prefix.
requirements: Both input pointers must be non-null and point to NUL-terminated strings

functions.name: doublenul
functions.description: Locates or validates a double-NUL-terminated sequence within a buffer. Returns a pointer related to the double-NUL boundary. Exact behavior is not documented in this header; infer that it operates on a buffer of specified length that contains two consecutive NUL bytes.
requirements: The first parameter must point to a buffer of at least the specified unsigned length
The buffer may contain one or more NUL-terminated substrings; the function likely expects a double-NUL terminator within the given length
Returned pointer semantics are unspecified; consult implementation before dereferencing

functions.name: readansi
functions.description: Reads data from a file descriptor into a buffer, likely with handling for ANSI escape sequences or interruption. Returns the number of bytes read or a negative value on error.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor for reading
buf must point to writable memory of at least size bytes
May perform partial reads; returned value should be checked for 0 (EOF) and -1 (error)
Thread and signal interruption behavior is unspecified; name suggests special handling of ANSI or EINTR

functions.name: FormatInt64
functions.description: Formats a signed 64-bit integer into a provided character buffer, producing a NUL-terminated textual representation. Returns a pointer (likely to the end of the written string).
requirements: Buffer must be large enough to hold the formatted number and terminating NUL
The return pointer location semantics (start vs. end) are not documented; verify before use

functions.name: FormatUint64
functions.description: Formats an unsigned 64-bit integer into a provided character buffer, producing a NUL-terminated textual representation. Returns a pointer (likely to the end of the written string).
requirements: Buffer must be large enough to hold the formatted number and terminating NUL
The return pointer location semantics (start vs. end) are not documented; verify before use

functions.name: FormatInt64Thousands
functions.description: Formats a signed 64-bit integer with thousands separators into a provided buffer. Returns a pointer (likely to the end of the written string).
requirements: Buffer must be sufficiently large for digits, separators, optional sign, and terminating NUL
Separator style/localization not documented; likely fixed

functions.name: FormatUint64Thousands
functions.description: Formats an unsigned 64-bit integer with thousands separators into a provided buffer. Returns a pointer (likely to the end of the written string).
requirements: Buffer must be sufficiently large for digits, separators, and terminating NUL
Separator style/localization not documented; likely fixed

functions.name: FormatSize
functions.description: Formats a size value into human-readable form, likely using a specified base or unit step given by the third argument. Returns a pointer (likely to the end of the written string). Exact unit behavior is not documented.
requirements: Buffer must be large enough to hold the formatted size string
Second and third arguments must be valid size/unit values; exact constraints are unspecified

functions.name: Commandv
functions.description: Searches for an executable in PATH and writes the resolved path into the provided buffer, similar to command -v/which. Returns the output buffer pointer on success or possibly NULL on failure.
requirements: prog must be a non-null NUL-terminated string naming the program
out buffer must be non-null and have size bytes of writable space
The caller should check for NULL return to detect failure

functions.name: Demangle
functions.description: Demangles a C++ (or toolchain) mangled symbol name into a human-readable form and writes it into the provided buffer. Returns the output buffer pointer.
requirements: out buffer must be non-null and have at least size bytes of writable space
input mangled name must be a non-null NUL-terminated string
Demangling semantics depend on supported ABI; unsupported names may be copied or simplified

functions.name: Deflate
functions.description: Compresses a buffer using a deflate-like algorithm. Returns a pointer to the compressed data; writes the compressed size to the output length pointer.
requirements: src must be a non-null pointer to at least srclen bytes (second argument)
out_len must be a non-null pointer where the compressed size will be written
Returned buffer ownership is likely heap-allocated and must be freed by the caller (exact allocator not documented)
Compression format/details are not documented; interoperability unspecified

functions.name: Inflate
functions.signature: void Inflate(void *, unsigned, const void *, unsigned);
functions.description: Decompresses deflated data into a caller-provided output buffer. Does not return a value; errors/size mismatches behavior is not documented.
requirements: dst must be a non-null pointer to a buffer of at least dstlen bytes (second argument)
src must be a non-null pointer to at least srclen bytes (fourth argument)
The caller must ensure the destination buffer is large enough for the decompressed data; there is no return value to indicate truncation or failure in this signature

functions.name: UninterruptibleWrite
functions.description: Writes the entire buffer to a file descriptor, retrying short writes and interruptions (e.g., EINTR) until completion or a non-recoverable error. Returns total bytes written or -1 on failure.
requirements: fd must be a valid writable file descriptor
buf must point to at least count bytes readable by the process
May block until all data is written; callers should be prepared for blocking behavior
On error, returns -1 and sets errno (behavior typical but not documented)

functions.name: IsProcessTainted
functions.description: Returns a flag indicating whether the process environment/state is considered 'tainted' (e.g., due to setuid, env vars, or other conditions). Exact definition of taint is not documented here.
requirements: No arguments; callers should treat nonzero as tainted and zero as not tainted, but exact semantics are unspecified

functions.name: Magikarp
functions.description: Performs an operation over a byte buffer of the given length and returns a long. The exact purpose (hashing, randomization, transformation) is not documented in this header.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer to at least len bytes
len may be zero or positive; negative handling is unspecified
The function may modify the buffer; treat contents as mutable

functions.name: GetCpuCount
functions.description: Returns the number of logical CPUs available on the system.
requirements: No arguments; returns a positive count on success, or possibly a fallback/default if detection fails (unspecified)

functions.name: strchrnul_
functions.description: GNU extension: returns a pointer to the first occurrence of a character in a string, or to the terminating NUL byte if the character is not found.
requirements: The input string pointer must be non-null and point to a NUL-terminated string
The int character is interpreted as an unsigned char for matching

functions.name: vasprintf_
functions.description: Allocates a new string large enough to hold the formatted output produced by the format string and argument list. Stores the pointer in *strp and returns the number of characters printed (excluding the NUL) or a negative value on error.
requirements: strp must be a non-null pointer to a char* lvalue; on success, *strp points to a heap-allocated NUL-terminated string that the caller must free
fmt must be a non-null NUL-terminated format string
ap must be a valid initialized va_list for the format
On failure, *strp may be set to NULL; caller must check return value

functions.name: realpath_
functions.description: Resolves a pathname to an absolute canonical path. If the second argument is non-null, writes the result there; otherwise may allocate a buffer and return it. Behavior mirrors POSIX realpath().
requirements: path must be a non-null NUL-terminated string
If resolved is non-null, it must point to a writable buffer of at least PATH_MAX bytes (exact required size unspecified)
If resolved is NULL, the function may allocate and return a new buffer that the caller must free
On error, returns NULL and sets errno (typical but not documented here)

functions.name: memccpy_
functions.description: Copies bytes from src to dst until either c is found in src or n bytes have been copied. If c is found, copying stops and a pointer to the next byte in dst is returned; otherwise NULL is returned. Mirrors memccpy().
requirements: dst must point to a writable buffer of at least n bytes
src must point to a readable buffer of at least n bytes
c is interpreted as an unsigned char value to match during copy
The memory regions must not overlap (as in standard memccpy)

functions.name: wcwidth_
functions.description: Determines the column width of a wide character when printed in a terminal. Mirrors wcwidth().
requirements: Input wchar_t should be a valid Unicode scalar value; invalid or non-printable characters may return -1

functions.name: Vigna
functions.description: Advances a 64-bit pseudo-random number generator state (likely Vigna's xorshift* family) and returns the next 64-bit value.
requirements: state must be a non-null pointer to an array of one u64 element holding the current PRNG state
State must be initialized to a nonzero seed before first use

functions.name: strchrnul
functions.description: Finds the first occurrence of the character c (converted to an unsigned char) in the C string s. If c is not found, returns a pointer to the string’s terminating null byte. Useful for scanning without needing a separate NULL check when not found.
requirements: s must point to a valid, NUL-terminated string readable up to and including its terminating '\0'.
c is an int but is interpreted as an unsigned char value when compared.
The returned pointer will be within the bounds of s (either at the matching character or at the terminating '\0').
s must not be NULL.

functions.name: vasprintf
functions.signature: int vasprintf(char **strp, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: Formats a string according to fmt and arguments in ap, allocating a new buffer to hold the result and storing its address in *strp. Returns the number of characters printed (excluding the terminating null byte) on success, or a negative value on error. Typical usage mirrors GNU vasprintf; caller frees *strp on success.
requirements: strp must be non-NULL and point to a writable char* variable.
On success, *strp will point to a newly allocated, NUL-terminated string that the caller must free (usually with free()).
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string; arguments described by fmt must be present in ap and have matching types.
ap must be an initialized va_list corresponding to the arguments for fmt; it is indeterminate to reuse ap after this call unless copied with va_copy beforehand.
On error, the function returns a negative value (commonly -1) and typically sets *strp to NULL; callers must check the return value before using *strp.

functions.name: realpath
functions.description: Resolves path to an absolute, canonical pathname by expanding symlinks, relative components, and removing redundant separators. If resolved_path is non-NULL, the resolved path is written there; otherwise, a new buffer is allocated and returned. Returns the resolved path on success or NULL on failure (errno is typically set).
requirements: path must be a non-NULL C string.
If resolved_path is non-NULL, it must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the absolute path (traditionally at least PATH_MAX bytes) including the terminating '\0'.
If resolved_path is NULL, the function may allocate a new buffer for the result; the caller must free the returned pointer on success.
Caller must check for a NULL return to detect errors before using the result; on error, errno is typically set to indicate the cause.
The contents of resolved_path are undefined on error.

functions.name: memccpy
functions.signature: void *memccpy(void *restrict dest, const void *restrict src, int c, size_t n);
functions.description: Copies bytes from src to dest until either n bytes have been copied or the byte c (converted to unsigned char) is found in src; if c is found, copying stops after copying that byte and a pointer to the byte after the copy in dest is returned. If c is not found within n bytes, returns NULL.
requirements: dest must point to a writable memory region large enough for up to n bytes.
src must point to a readable memory region of at least n bytes (unless the copy stops earlier due to encountering c).
The memory regions referenced by dest and src must not overlap; behavior is undefined on overlap (like memcpy).
c is interpreted as an unsigned char value when searching.
The caller must check the return value: non-NULL indicates c was found and provides the position just past the copied c in dest; NULL indicates c was not found within the first n bytes.

functions.name: wcwidth
functions.description: Determines the number of column positions needed for the wide character wc when printed in a terminal; returns 0 for the null wide character, a non-negative width for printable characters, or -1 for nonprintable/unsupported characters. Behavior may be locale-dependent.
requirements: wc should be a valid wchar_t code point as interpreted under the current locale.
Return value -1 indicates a nonprintable character; callers should handle this case appropriately when computing display widths.
Locale settings may affect the result; ensure the desired locale is set (e.g., via setlocale) before calling if locale-dependent behavior is required.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid NUL-terminated C strings tailored to the fuzzer
# stubs that request FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for various APIs like EndsWith, StartsWith,
# Commandv, Demangle, GetOpt, and strchrnul variants.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a small corpus of interesting strings covering prefixes/suffixes,
#   typical command names, mangled-looking symbols, getopt-like arguments, and
#   edge cases (empty before NUL, long, punctuation, Unicode in UTF-8, etc.).
# - Randomly select and sometimes compose multiple strings separated by spaces
#   or path separators to exercise tokenization and parsing behaviors in the
#   targets. The fuzzer stubs will append a trailing NUL; here we return raw
#   bytes with a single NUL terminator to be valid on first use in file-backed
#   inputs as well.
# - Keep total size under 4096 bytes.
#
# Note: The environment will call this generator to obtain a single fuzz buffer
# that seeds FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. We therefore pack one or more
# NUL-terminated C strings into a single buffer, separated by single NUL bytes,
# so multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls can each consume a distinct string if the
# harness supports splitting on NUL. If not, each consumer at least sees a
# valid C string prefix.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Interesting building blocks
CMD_NAMES = [
    b"sh", b"bash", b"zsh", b"dash", b"python3", b"ls", b"cat", b"echo",
    b"grep", b"sed", b"awk", b"env", b"true", b"false", b"make", b"cc", b"clang",
]
PATH_LIKE = [
    b"/bin/sh", b"/usr/bin/env", b"/usr/bin/python3", b"/bin/echo", b"/sbin/ldconfig",
    b"./configure", b"../script.sh", b"/nonexistent/cmd", b"/tmp/a.out",
]
MANGLED_LIKE = [
    b"_Z3foov", b"_ZN3abc5Inner3barEi", b"_ZSt4cout", b"_ZdlPv", b"_ZTIi",
    b"_Z1fv", b"_Z7examplePcS_", b"_ZNSt6vectorIiSaIiEE6resizeEm", b"_GLOBAL__sub_I_foo",
]
GETOPT_ARGS = [
    b"-a", b"-b", b"-cvalue", b"-d", b"-e123", b"--long", b"--help", b"-h",
    b"-Iinclude", b"-Wall", b"-O2", b"-o", b"out.o", b"--", b"file.txt",
]
SUFFIXES = [b".c", b".cc", b".cpp", b".h", b".hpp", b".txt", b".md", b".so", b".a", b".tar.gz"]
PREFIXES = [b"lib", b"test_", b"tmp_", b"sample_", b"src/", b"build/"]
UNICODE_UTF8 = [
    "π", "✓", "汉字", "🚀", "élan", "naïve", "Ω", "€", "日本語", "русский"
]
SPECIALS = [b"", b" ", b"\t", b"\n", b"--", b"-", b"/", b".", b"..", b"./", b"../"]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, alphabet: bytes) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    alpha = (string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./:+,= ").encode()
    return _rand_bytes(rng, min_len, max_len, alpha)


def _maybe_append_suffix(rng: random.Random, s: bytes) -> bytes:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s += rng.choice(SUFFIXES)
    return s


def _maybe_prepend_prefix(rng: random.Random, s: bytes) -> bytes:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = rng.choice(PREFIXES) + s
    return s


def _make_prog(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Sometimes a bare command, sometimes a path-like program
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = rng.choice(CMD_NAMES)
    else:
        s = rng.choice(PATH_LIKE)
    # Occasionally decorate with prefix/suffix to exercise EndsWith/StartsWith
    s = _maybe_prepend_prefix(rng, s)
    s = _maybe_append_suffix(rng, s)
    return s


def _make_mangled(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    base = rng.choice(MANGLED_LIKE)
    # Occasionally add a space or surrounding noise; demanglers should still see the token
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base = b" " + base + b" "
    return base


def _make_getopt_argv(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # argc in [1,5]; first arg is program name
    argc = rng.randint(1, 5)
    argv: List[bytes] = []
    argv.append(_make_prog(rng))
    for _ in range(argc - 1):
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            argv.append(rng.choice(GETOPT_ARGS))
        else:
            argv.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 8))
    return argv


def _make_optstring(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Include mix of flags with and without ':' to require arguments
    opts = []
    letters = "abcdefghiopqrstuvwxy"
    for ch in letters:
        if rng.random() < 0.25:
            opts.append(ch)
            if rng.random() < 0.4:
                opts.append(":")
    if not opts:
        opts = list("a:")
    return ("".join(opts)).encode()


def _make_ends_starts_pair(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Create a base string and a suffix/prefix that often matches
    base = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 32)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        suf = rng.choice(SUFFIXES)
        pre = rng.choice(PREFIXES)
        a = pre + base + suf
        b_end = suf if rng.random() < 0.7 else _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 6)
        b_start = pre if rng.random() < 0.7 else _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 6)
        return [a, b_end, a, b_start]
    else:
        # Random mismatching pairs
        return [
            _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 24), _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 8),
            _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 24), _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 8),
        ]


def _make_strchrnul_case(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    s = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 40)
    # Occasionally include the searched character to hit both branches in strchrnul
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s += bytes([rng.randint(0, 255)])
    return s


def _make_unicode_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    text = rng.choice(UNICODE_UTF8)
    # Surround with ASCII noise to test mixed UTF-8/ASCII
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        text = rng.choice(["lib", "test_", "src/"]) + text
    return text.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")


def _pack_cstrings(strings: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Pack multiple C strings separated by single NULs and ensure final NUL
    parts = []
    total = 0
    for s in strings:
        # Ensure no embedded NULs in components to preserve whole-string semantics
        s = s.split(b"\x00")[0]
        if total + len(s) + 1 > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        parts.append(s + b"\x00")
        total += len(s) + 1
    if not parts:
        parts = [b"a\x00"]
    blob = b"".join(parts)
    # Ensure the blob ends with a NUL
    if not blob or blob[-1] != 0:
        blob += b"\x00"
    return blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    strings: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) For Commandv: a likely program token
    strings.append(_make_prog(rng))

    # 2) For Demangle: a mangled-like symbol
    strings.append(_make_mangled(rng))

    # 3) For GetOpt: argv array flattened as separate C strings, plus optstring
    argv = _make_getopt_argv(rng)
    strings.extend(argv)
    strings.append(_make_optstring(rng))

    # 4) For EndsWith/StartsWith: include pairs to often produce true and false
    pair = _make_ends_starts_pair(rng)
    strings.extend(pair)

    # 5) For strchrnul cases
    strings.append(_make_strchrnul_case(rng))

    # 6) Unicode-rich token to exercise UTF-8 handling in generic string paths
    strings.append(_make_unicode_blob(rng))

    # 7) Sprinkle specials to test edge cases (empty, dot paths, etc.)
    strings.append(rng.choice(SPECIALS))

    return _pack_cstrings(strings)

import random
import os
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for arbitrary binary data used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME in the target stub.
# Target stub writes up to 256 bytes to stderr via UninterruptibleWrite. Our goal is to
# produce interesting, valid byte buffers covering diverse sizes and byte patterns.

MAX_OUTPUT = 4096
MAX_STUB_SIZE = 256  # stub truncates to 256; keep payloads within a reasonable bound


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix printable, whitespace, nulls, and high bytes
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        mode = rng.randrange(8)
        remain = n - i
        if mode == 0:
            # ASCII letters/digits
            k = min(remain, rng.randint(1, 32))
            pool = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789"
            chunks.append(bytes(pool[rng.randrange(len(pool))] for _ in range(k)))
            i += k
        elif mode == 1:
            # Zero bytes run
            k = min(remain, rng.randint(1, 64))
            chunks.append(b"\x00" * k)
            i += k
        elif mode == 2:
            # High bytes run (OS entropy)
            k = min(remain, rng.randint(1, 32))
            chunks.append(os.urandom(k))
            i += k
        elif mode == 3:
            # Repeated byte
            k = min(remain, rng.randint(1, 64))
            bval = rng.randrange(256)
            chunks.append(bytes([bval]) * k)
            i += k
        elif mode == 4:
            # Whitespace and control
            k = min(remain, rng.randint(1, 32))
            pool = b" \t\r\n\v\f\x1b"  # include ESC
            chunks.append(bytes(pool[rng.randrange(len(pool))] for _ in range(k)))
            i += k
        elif mode == 5:
            # Structured prefixes/suffixes to vary terminal/stdio behavior
            s = rng.choice([
                b"", b"\x00", b"\x00\x00", b"\xff\x00\xff", b"\x1b[31m", b"\x1b[0m",
                b"BEGIN", b"END", b"\n", b"\r\n"
            ])
            k = min(remain, len(s))
            chunks.append(s[:k])
            i += k
        elif mode == 6:
            # Small integers in various endianness (only valid sizes 2/4/8)
            if remain >= 8 and rng.random() < 0.34:
                k = 8
            elif remain >= 4 and rng.random() < 0.5:
                k = 4
            elif remain >= 2:
                k = 2
            else:
                # Not enough space; fall back to single random bytes
                k = min(remain, 1)
                chunks.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(k)))
                i += k
                continue
            val = rng.getrandbits(k * 8)
            endian = rng.choice(['<', '>'])
            fmt = {2: 'H', 4: 'I', 8: 'Q'}[k]
            chunks.append(struct.pack(endian + fmt, val))
            i += k
        else:
            # Random single bytes
            k = min(remain, rng.randint(1, 32))
            chunks.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(k)))
            i += k
    return b"".join(chunks)


def _interesting_sizes(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Sizes that may trigger edge paths in write loops
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 191, 192, 255, 256]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(choices)
    # Otherwise a random size within stub limit
    return rng.randint(0, MAX_STUB_SIZE)


def _compose_payload(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    # Compose payload from several segments to increase diversity
    if size <= 0:
        return b""
    segments: List[bytes] = []
    remaining = size
    while remaining > 0:
        # bias to mixed segment sizes
        seg_len = min(remaining, max(1, int(rng.triangular(1, min(64, remaining), 8))))
        segments.append(_rand_bytes(rng, seg_len))
        remaining -= seg_len
    return b"".join(segments)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Determine final size respecting both stub limit and global max
    size = _interesting_sizes(rng)
    size = min(size, MAX_STUB_SIZE)

    payload = _compose_payload(rng, size)

    # Occasionally craft special-case payloads with semantics that can affect terminal/stdio behavior
    # without making them invalid.
    if size > 0 and rng.random() < 0.25:
        choice = rng.randrange(6)
        if choice == 0:
            # Pure zeros
            payload = b"\x00" * size
        elif choice == 1:
            # Newline-heavy
            if size >= 5:
                payload = (b"line\n" * (size // 5)) + b"\n" * (size % 5)
            else:
                payload = b"\n" * size
        elif choice == 2:
            # Carriage-return + newline patterns
            unit = b"\r\n"
            payload = (unit * (size // len(unit))) + unit[: size % len(unit)]
        elif choice == 3:
            # ANSI color codes surrounding random data
            core_len = max(0, size - 8)
            core = _compose_payload(rng, core_len)
            payload = (b"\x1b[31m" + core + b"\x1b[0m")[:size]
        elif choice == 4:
            # Alternating high/low bytes
            payload = bytes((0xff if (i & 1) else 0x00) for i in range(size))
        elif choice == 5:
            # Incrementing bytes
            start = rng.randrange(256)
            payload = bytes((start + i) & 0xff for i in range(size))

    # Ensure global cap
    if len(payload) > MAX_OUTPUT:
        payload = payload[:MAX_OUTPUT]

    return payload

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces on-disk file contents and a filename path string
# (returned as bytes) for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME-based fuzzers that call realpath/realpath_.
#
# Strategy:
# - Emit a valid NUL-terminated absolute or relative path as the buffer.
# - The harness will create a file with this name containing the same buffer data
#   (framework behavior). We therefore include a variety of directory structures
#   and path patterns to exercise realpath canonicalization:
#   - Absolute vs relative
#   - Dot and dot-dot segments
#   - Redundant slashes
#   - Trailing slashes
#   - Long components and near-PATH_MAX lengths but <= 4096
#   - Mix of ASCII, spaces, special but common filename chars
#
# We ensure the produced path is a single NUL-terminated string <=4096 bytes.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ .,@+%!^(){}[]"

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
PATH_MAXISH = 3500  # keep well under 4096 while allowing long paths


def _rand(r: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return r.randint(a, b)


def _rand_choice(r: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]


def _make_component(r: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 16) -> str:
    n = _rand(r, min_len, max_len)
    # Avoid empty and single dot unless explicitly chosen elsewhere
    s = ''.join(_rand_choice(r, SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n)).strip()
    # Avoid component becoming empty after strip
    if not s:
        s = 'x'
    # Avoid reserved names like '.' or '..' here
    if s in ('.', '..'):
        s = 'x' + s.replace('.', 'x')
    return s


def _dotdot_rich_segments(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Return a mixture of ".", ".." and normal components
    segs = []
    count = _rand(r, 1, 8)
    for _ in range(count):
        t = _rand(r, 0, 4)
        if t == 0:
            segs.append('.')
        elif t == 1:
            segs.append('..')
        else:
            segs.append(_make_component(r))
    return segs


def _long_component(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    n = max(1, target_len)
    return ''.join(_rand_choice(r, SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _maybe_trailing_slash(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return '/' if r.random() < 0.3 else ''


def _join_with_redundant_seps(r: random.Random, parts: List[str]) -> str:
    # Insert random multiple slashes between parts to test collapse
    if not parts:
        return '/'
    path = parts[0]
    for p in parts[1:]:
        seps = '/' * _rand(r, 1, 3)  # one to three slashes
        path += seps + p
    return path


def _abs_path_cases(r: random.Random) -> str:
    style = _rand(r, 0, 6)
    if style == 0:
        # Simple absolute with few components
        comps = [_make_component(r) for _ in range(_rand(r, 1, 5))]
        p = '/' + _join_with_redundant_seps(r, comps)
    elif style == 1:
        # Absolute with dot/dotdot mixture
        comps = _dotdot_rich_segments(r)
        p = '/' + _join_with_redundant_seps(r, comps)
    elif style == 2:
        # Absolute with trailing slash
        comps = [_make_component(r) for _ in range(_rand(r, 1, 6))]
        p = '/' + '/'.join(comps) + _maybe_trailing_slash(r)
    elif style == 3:
        # Absolute with redundant leading slashes
        leading = '/' * _rand(r, 2, 5)
        comps = [_make_component(r) for _ in range(_rand(r, 1, 5))]
        p = leading + '/'.join(comps)
    elif style == 4:
        # Absolute with very long last component
        comps = [_make_component(r) for _ in range(_rand(r, 1, 4))]
        # choose long component length but respect total size limit later
        long_len = _rand(r, 64, 512)
        comps.append(_long_component(r, long_len))
        p = '/' + '/'.join(comps)
    else:
        # Absolute root or root with single dot/dotdot
        p = '/' + _rand_choice(r, ['.', '..'])
    # Possibly append extra redundant slashes
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        p += '/' * _rand(r, 2, 4)
    return p


def _rel_path_cases(r: random.Random) -> str:
    style = _rand(r, 0, 6)
    if style == 0:
        comps = [_make_component(r) for _ in range(_rand(r, 1, 5))]
        p = _join_with_redundant_seps(r, comps)
    elif style == 1:
        comps = _dotdot_rich_segments(r)
        p = _join_with_redundant_seps(r, comps)
    elif style == 2:
        p = './' + _join_with_redundant_seps(r, [_make_component(r) for _ in range(_rand(r, 1, 5))])
    elif style == 3:
        p = '../' * _rand(r, 1, 6) + _make_component(r)
    elif style == 4:
        comps = [_make_component(r) for _ in range(_rand(r, 2, 8))]
        p = '/'.join(comps) + _maybe_trailing_slash(r)
    else:
        # Single component relative
        p = _make_component(r)
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        p += '/' * _rand(r, 2, 4)
    return p


def _pad_to_limit(r: random.Random, p: str) -> str:
    # Occasionally generate very long but valid paths by appending more components
    if len(p) >= PATH_MAXISH or r.random() < 0.6:
        return p
    # Try to extend up to PATH_MAXISH without exceeding MAX_TOTAL-1 (for NUL)
    target = _rand(r, min(PATH_MAXISH, len(p)+1), PATH_MAXISH)
    while len(p) < target:
        comp_len = _rand(r, 1, 24)
        comp = _long_component(r, comp_len)
        candidate = p + ('/' if not p.endswith('/') else '') + comp
        if len(candidate) >= MAX_TOTAL - 1:
            break
        p = candidate
    return p


def _make_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        p = _abs_path_cases(r)
    else:
        p = _rel_path_cases(r)
    p = _pad_to_limit(r, p)
    # Ensure non-empty and not exceeding limits
    if not p:
        p = '/'
    if len(p) > MAX_TOTAL - 1:
        p = p[:MAX_TOTAL - 1]
    return p


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    path = _make_path(r)
    # Ensure NUL-terminated bytes for C string expectation
    b = path.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')[:MAX_TOTAL - 1] + b'\x00'
    return b
